Sawstop is a company created to market an invention patented by Steve Gass. The bottom line is that it works like one of those touch lamps, except instead of turning on a lamp it retracts a buzz saw under the table, possibly saving your fingers. The downsides?

  • The guy owns a patent on the technology and sues anyone who tries to make anything similar. Including a development which achieved the same thing without destroying the saw blade.

Despite all this he's campaigning for the invention to be made mandatory on all table saws and NPR are happy to give his whining a greater audience without even the slightest bit of context or counterargument.

The saw blade is stopped by a block of aluminum being jammed forcibly into the teeth of the saw blade. Both the aluminum block and the saw blade are ruined and must be replaced after activation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SawStop

According to SawStop, the system has restrictions and limitations:[6]

  • The braking system must be deactivated when cutting very green or wet timber.
  • Non-conductive blades or blades with non-conductive hubs or teeth cannot be used.
  • The braking system is designed to work with kerfs from 3/32″ to 3/16″; using thinner or thicker kerfs limits the saw's ability to stop the blade after accidental contact, likely resulting in more serious injury.
